Getting started with backyardWTC

getting-started.Rmd

What the package does

backyardWTC is an R package and Shiny dashboard for exploring a snapshot of stopped runners from the 2026 Backyard Ultra World Team Championships. It is intended for spectators, running enthusiasts and performance analysts asking how completed-yard performance differs across nations and competition classes.

The included wtc_stopped dataset records 925 stopped runners from 67 nations in four classes, captured after yard 124. One yard means one completed race lap. The data is not the complete starting field, live race standings or the final team results.

Install and launch

Install the package from its GitHub Classroom repository:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-jban0020")

Load it and launch the application:

library(backyardWTC)
run_wtc_app()

The Shiny app reads the dataset from the installed package. You do not need to download or load the original CSV to run it.

The two dashboard tabs

The app offers Race progression and Performance comparison. Each tab has its own nation, competition-class and yard controls. Changing the filters in one tab does not change the other tab.

Race progression: when do runners stop?

Use this tab to reconstruct how the recorded stopped-runner cohort progresses through completed-yard thresholds.

  1. Choose any nations, or leave the nation selection blank for all nations. Tick the classes to include.
  2. Move the Current completed yard slider, use the previous/next buttons, or play the slider to move one yard at a time.
  3. Select Runners reaching each yard for a cumulative count, or Stopped at each yard to examine departures.
  4. Click a chart point or bar to update the selected yard and see the runner names and recorded stopping reasons. The table initially shows eight runners and can be expanded.

The metric Reached at least yard X counts runners who completed X or more yards. For example, a runner recorded with exactly 50 completed yards is counted as having reached yard 50, but not yard 51. A flat section of the progression chart means no runner in the selected cohort stopped at that completed-yard count.

This is not a survival curve for the entire field: runners not recorded as stopped in this snapshot are outside the dataset.

Performance comparison: how do groups differ?

Use this tab to compare nations or competition classes, with filters that are separate from those in Race progression.

  1. Set Compare performance by to Nation or Competition class and choose which nations and classes are included.
  2. Select Total yards (lines) to plot each group’s cumulative completed yards through every yard threshold. The yard slider highlights one vertical position on these lines; it does not filter the lines. Runners left in the hover details refers only to the selected stopped-runner cohort reaching that threshold and does not set line height.
  3. Switch to Runner distribution to see individual stopped-runner yard counts and box plots for each group. Here the yard slider is a minimum completed-yards filter.
  4. Choose Median yards or Mean yards to rank the summary table, then show the top five groups, selected groups or all groups. In Nation mode you can also choose how many nations appear in the chart.

The plotted groups and table can use different rankings: line-chart nations are selected by total accumulated yards, while table rows are ranked by the selected mean or median. Total yards is strongly affected by the number of runners in the group; mean and median are better for discussing typical individual performance. Very small groups can give unstable comparisons.

Interpreting a result

For example, choose all nations and all classes, then compare the classes using the summary table. In this snapshot, the median recorded completion was 62.5 yards for Super Six versus 18 yards for Class A. These are comparisons within the recorded stopped-runner data, not causal effects of class membership or official team rankings. The class definitions are source-recorded categories, and the dataset does not by itself establish why they differ.

The Race progression tab supports a complementary question: at what point did runners in the chosen cohort tend to stop, and were there yards with more recorded stops than others? Use the chart’s tooltips and stopping-details table to connect the counts with the individual records.

Summarise the data in R

The wtc_stopped dataset can be explored without the app:

head(wtc_stopped[, c("runner", "nation", "class", "yards")])
#>            runner                   nation     class yards
#> 1    Ivo Steyaert                  Belgium Super Six   124
#> 2   Merijn Geerts                  Belgium Super Six   124
#> 3        Jon Noll United States of America Super Six   106
#> 4 Kengo Takahashi                    Japan Super Six   104
#> 5  Julien Pierlot                   France Super Six   100
#> 6  Nicholas Steel United States of America Super Six    94

The exported summarise_stopped_runners() function is also used by the app to calculate grouped statistics. It returns group size, mean and median yards, maximum yards and total yards.

summarise_stopped_runners(group = "class")
#>       group runners mean_yards median_yards max_yards total_yards
#> 1 Super Six      84   64.58333         62.5       124        5425
#> 2 Class AAA     252   40.85317         38.0        89       10295
#> 3  Class AA     278   28.85612         29.0        61        8022
#> 4   Class A     311   18.92283         18.0        42        5885

To compare nations among runners completing at least 50 yards:

head(summarise_stopped_runners(group = "nation", min_yards = 50))
#>                      group runners mean_yards median_yards max_yards
#> 1 United States of America      11   79.81818         83.0       106
#> 2                Australia      13   72.46154         73.0        86
#> 3                   Mexico       2   70.50000         70.5        72
#> 4           United Kingdom      10   68.70000         69.0        89
#> 5              New Zealand       8   65.12500         67.5        76
#> 6                  Belgium      13   74.69231         67.0       124
#>   total_yards
#> 1         878
#> 2         942
#> 3         141
#> 4         687
#> 5         521
#> 6         971

Empty selections and limitations

If you uncheck every competition class, the app explains that no runners match rather than displaying a misleading chart. In Performance comparison, selecting a minimum yard threshold above every runner in the selected group also produces an informative message. Broaden the selection or lower the threshold to continue.

The data comes from the WTC 2026 Live Dashboard, captured as a CSV snapshot after yard 124. It contains 925 stopped runners across 67 nations, not all competitors. It cannot be used to infer complete final standings, and comparing nations with different numbers of runners requires care.

Further information

See ?wtc_stopped for the data dictionary, ?summarise_stopped_runners for the summary function and ?run_wtc_app for the app launcher.
